explanation:
## How the puzzle works

**What the grid contains.** Each input has one big shape made of colour 7. It also has one or two single 2-cells sitting on the border of the grid. These 2-cells are markers.

**Evidence from the demonstrations.**

- **Pair 3.** The marker is at the bottom, at (17,9), so it controls column 9.
  - In the output, column 9 is drawn in 2 from the marker up to the shape. The shape's own cells in that column, (10,9) and (11,9), stay 7.
  - Everything left of column 9 is moved as one rigid block into the bottom-left corner. Its bounding box ends up touching both the bottom and left edges.
  - Everything right of column 9 is moved the same way into the bottom-right corner.
- **Pair 2.** The marker is at the top, at (0,9).
  - Column 9 has shape cells at rows 4, 5, 9 and 10. The line is 2 from the marker all the way to the farthest shape cell (row 10), but the shape cells inside that stretch stay 7. That gives the pattern 2,2,2,2,7,7,2,2,2,7,7.
  - The two side pieces go to the top-left and top-right corners.
- **Pair 1.** There are two markers: one on the top edge (column 8) and one on the right edge (row 8).
  - Both lines are drawn. Where they cross, (8,8), the cell is 2.
  - The lines cut the shape into four quadrants. Each quadrant goes to its own corner as a rigid block. For example, the top-left piece spans bbox rows 4–7, cols 4–7 and lands at rows 0–3, cols 0–3. I checked the top-right and bottom-right pieces in the same way.
  - The bottom-left quadrant touches neither marker edge, and it disappears from the output.

**Rule.**
1. For each border marker, draw a 2 line perpendicular to its edge. The line starts at the marker and runs to the farthest shape cell on that line. Shape cells along the way stay 7.
2. Take the shape cells that are not on a line. Group them by which side of each line they fall on.
3. Move each group rigidly so that its bounding box sits in the matching corner. "Matching" means the corner on the group's side of each line, combined with the marker's edge when there is only one line.
4. A group whose corner touches no marker edge is deleted. This only happens in the two-marker case.

**Test input.** The marker is at (19,8) on the bottom edge, so it controls column 8.
- Column 8 is drawn in 2 from row 19 up to the topmost shape cell in that column, (6,8), which stays 7.
- The shape cells left of column 8 move rigidly to the bottom-left corner.
- The shape cells right of column 8 move rigidly to the bottom-right corner.

The program implements this and checks itself only through the harness.
